brief: Bitcoin's seasonal 'Uptober' rally inverted in 2026: BTC fell 7.4% to $77,401, ETH fell 16.2%, and SOL fell 19.3%, while US spot ETFs for the three saw a combined $2.3bn outflow. Most of the drop came after North Korea's $6.3bn hack of Binance. Goldman's Kenny Lee notes ETH's ETF demand was weakening before the hack, so the breach accelerated a trend rather than caused it. BTC's MVRV ratio of 1.43 implies a 30% cushion above its $54,000 cost basis. ETH's MVRV of 1.02 is near breakeven at its $2,213 cost basis. Derivatives barely reacted: open interest fell only 0.55% against a 3.66% price drop and funding held near 10%, which Goldman reads as leveraged traders buying the dip, not cutting risk. Separately, TD Cowen's Seiberg calls a Democratic Senate sweep, giving Warren the Banking gavel, the worst outcome for crypto regulation, worse than a split or Republican Senate. He and Bernstein note regulators can still favor the industry by executive action regardless of Congress. Bloomberg's survey put median year-end BTC at $76,456 under a Democratic sweep, against bitcoin's $77,401 close, meaning the scenario looks priced in. Zero Hedge expects more downside if ETH's cost basis breaks.
